To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have constructed and compared the genetic and epgenetic networks of embryonic stem (ES) cells and HeLa cells, and have found that the specific genetic networks of HeLa cells are involved in the carcinogenesis of cervical cancer, which could lead to the identification of new drugs for cancer treatment.

we have constructed the real GECNs for ESCs and HeLa cells by using big databases and genome high throughput sequencing data, and have identified potential carcinogenic and drug design mechanisms for cervical cancer.
we have identified core GECNs and common and specific GECN modules of HeLa cells for systems cancer drug discovery.

the identification of the genetic and ep genetic networks of HeLa cells, the investigation of the carcinogenic and stem ness mechanisms of HeLa cells by integrating the specific GECN of HeLa cells with drug databases, and the identification of drugs for cervical cancer therapy with minimal side effects.

the core GECN of HeLa cancer cells could be a potential drug target for cancer treatment with minimal toxicity on the common core genes of ESCs.

we could identify potential carcinogenic and anti carcinogenic mechanisms for systems cancer drugs by integrating big database mining with next generation sequencing data.

big database mining, system modeling, and system identification could be used to identify core GECNs and their specific genes in cancer and stem cells for cancer drug design with minimal side effects and for stem cell differentiation.
